newsitem.title: USA: U.S. job cuts soar 62 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. job cuts soar 62 percent in October.

text.p: U.S. job cuts soared more than 60 percent last month to the highest level since January, an outplacement firm said Wednesday, in another sign that the economy was slowing.

Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc. said that layoffs in October totalled 47,911, up 62 percent from September's 29,632. The October total was the highest since 97,379 in January, and also was the highest October number since 1993, when 66,801 people were thrown out of work.
The job-cut total for the year to date of 410,208 is about 20 percent above the year-ago level of 342,824, it said.

"The October job cut number is further confirmation that the economy has cooled off since the summer and that the forces driving downsizing -- technology, deregulation, cost-cutting, free-trade and reengineering -- remain undiminished," said John Challenger, executive vice president at the international outplacement firm.

The monthly survey also ties in with last week's government report that the economy braked hard in the third quarter, showing a growth rate of only 2.2 percent after speeding ahead at 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
Also last Friday, the Labour Department said the unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, as the economy started producing new jobs at a healthy pace.

The department said services industries added 119,000 jobs -- the largest gain since May -- as amusement and recreation added jobs while industry in general showed fewer layoffs. Retail trade added 62,000 jobs in October.
Challenger said that in the battle for skilled employees, many smaller firms have been losing to bigger companies with deeper pockets.
"Larger firms now have the advantage of being able to shift personnel from one area to another, and therefore retain valued employees even in this period of uncertainty," Challenger said.
The October Challenger report said the retail sector suffered the most job cuts at 13,459. The job cuts were boosted by Best Products Co.'s decision to close its doors and lay off 10,000 workers.
The cuts at Richmond, Va.-based Best Products were the largest since 1993, when Sears Roebuck slashed 50,000 workers in January of that year and Woolworth Corp. laid off 13,000 in October.
Challenger said the sector with the second largest job losses in October was the insurance industry, which wiped out 8,276 jobs, automotive, 5,323 and transportation with 3,800 job cuts.
